title: Elasticsearch: Hadoop log lines arrive complete and well-formed (data quality)
summary: Loads 978 Hadoop container log files into the Elasticsearch index hadoop_logs and proves data quality: no empty documents, every line keeps its timestamp, level and message, line counts and level distribution match the source. Conditional routing (r088) is not built in OpenETL, so this checks data quality instead.

steps.title: Delete the hadoop_logs index
steps.explain: Starts clean so every document found later was written by this run.

steps.title: Scan the source Hadoop log files
steps.explain: Counts the real log lines, their levels and malformed lines in the 978 source files.

steps.title: Count documents in the index (Before)
steps.explain: Before the run the index does not exist, so it holds nothing.

steps.title: Run the es_hadoop_logs pipeline
steps.explain: Runs the real pipeline. Everything below checks what it produced.

steps.title: Job finished with status COMPLETED
steps.explain: PARTIAL means some part of the work failed.

steps.title: Job reported 0 warnings
steps.explain: Each warning is a file or step that went wrong.

steps.title: Count documents in the index (After)
steps.explain: The number of chunk documents Elasticsearch holds (each chunk packs many log lines).

steps.title: The index holds documents
steps.explain: An empty index would mean nothing was loaded.

steps.title: Scan every indexed document
steps.explain: Applies the same line rules to the indexed text as to the source files.

steps.title: No empty documents
steps.explain: A document without text is useless for search.

steps.title: Every document records its source file
steps.explain: Without source_filename a log line cannot be traced back.

steps.title: Every source file reached the index
steps.explain: Each of the source log files must appear as a source_filename.

steps.title: Every document holds at least one timestamped log entry
steps.explain: A document with no 'date time LEVEL message' line is not a usable log record.

steps.title: Only known log levels appear
steps.explain: Levels must come from TRACE DEBUG INFO WARN ERROR FATAL.

steps.title: INFO is the majority level
steps.explain: In healthy Hadoop job logs most entries are INFO.

steps.title: ERROR and FATAL are under 10 percent
steps.explain: A plausible distribution has few errors; a high share would mean misparsed levels.

steps.title: No log entry was lost
steps.explain: Indexed timestamped entries must be at least the source count.

steps.title: Stack-trace frames are all present
steps.explain: Every 'at class(file:line)' frame in the source must still be in the index text.

steps.title: Entry count equals the source exactly
steps.explain: Chunk overlap can repeat entries; equal counts mean nothing is duplicated.

steps.title: Line structure is preserved
steps.explain: Indexed non-blank line count equals the source; fewer lines means multi-line entries were merged.

steps.title: Level distribution equals the source
steps.explain: Indexed per-level counts must equal the source counts.
